gloss: to flatter; to coax; to butter up

definitions.explanation: To praise someone excessively, often insincerely, to put them in a good mood or get them to do something.

examples.japanese: {部下|ぶか}をおだてて{仕事|しごと}をさせる。
examples.english: To flatter subordinates into doing work.

examples.japanese: おだてられると{調子|ちょうし}に{乗|の}ってしまう。
examples.english: When flattered, I tend to get carried away.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}をおだてて{勉強|べんきょう}させようとしたが、{見抜|みぬ}かれた。
examples.english: I tried to coax the child into studying by flattering them, but they saw through it.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY:
Transitive verb (他動詞). The person being flattered takes を.

PROVERB:
・{豚|ぶた}もおだてりゃ{木|き}に{登|のぼ}る - Even a pig will climb a tree if you flatter it enough (flattery can motivate anyone)

COMPARISON:
・おだてる - to flatter (with insincere praise to get something)
・{褒|ほ}める - to praise (can be genuine)
・お{世辞|せじ}を{言|い}う - to pay compliments (formal flattery)
・{持|も}ち{上|あ}げる - to praise/elevate someone

USAGE NOTE:
Often implies the flattery is insincere or has an ulterior motive.
